0.0.n: Japanese nouns do not change for plural; here うさぎ refers to rabbits in general.

0.1.n: Pronounced わ, this particle marks rabbits as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: かわいい describes a quality, and adding です makes the statement polite.

1.0.n: Japanese nouns do not change for plural; here うさぎ refers to rabbits in general.

1.1.n: Pronounced わ, this particle marks rabbits as the topic of the sentence.

2.0.n: Japanese has no word for the article an here; 象 alone names the animal.

2.1.n: Pronounced お, this particle marks the elephant as what was seen.

2.2.n: 見ました is the polite past form of 見る; the speaker is understood as the person who saw it.

2.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when context makes it clear; here I is understood.
